    Tuesday 22 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    Three bets, not twenty: the chair ships a mega-cap long, a bank short worn once across three puts, and value holds - seven option legs on merit and three declared vacancies - on a 13:02 ET mark, under thirteen court rules that ran as code for the first time and a share median from which four seats were absent by rule

The bank-short cluster dies as one if the ten-year (4.98% [QUOTED=OVERNIGHT TAPE]) breaks lower and the sector squeezes from BAC's rsi_14 of 25.7 [QUOTED=candidate row]. EXE dies on a close over 92.88 [QUOTED=suggested_kill_level]. HOUSE RULES, set before the open of the remaining tape (freeze 13:02 ET [QUOTED=desk_brief.txt]). Stakes: share_default 1.0, option_default 0.5, per_line_cap 1.5 [QUOTED=columns.json]; AAPL 1.5 is the only line at the cap [QUOTED=columns.json stakes]; each cluster is sized as one bet - BAC 0.75 with USB 0.5 and WFC 0.35, INTC 0.75, TSLA and PLTR 0.35 as variance tickets [QUOTED=columns.json stakes]. Exit rules: every share line closes in the record at the next open after a close through its kill level, no intraday fires; every option leg follows its underlying's kill level. Ratchets on the high-variance legs (INTC, PLTR, MRK, TSLA): bank half above 2x, trail the rest 40% off the high [QUOTED=croupier ratchet]. Windfall policy: any leg over 2x [QUOTED=croupier ratchet] has half banked the session it prints; no stake is raised mid-session, no vacancy is filled mid-session, and the three option vacancies stay vacant tonight.

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder in its second session - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 13:04 ET, WITH 175 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    The court's report

    ADMISSIBLE: run 44 is judged and advisory, and the hole is the provider's while every defect this court found is the desk's. Sixteen of sixteen seats distinguished run 40 and the doctrine is settled as an information test, not a calendar one - but twelve of sixteen built their strongest challenge on a thirty-minute clock mismatch that disclosure 8's own bar labels rule out, and the defect they missed is proven in the digits: these closes are computed marks, not trade prints. R16a's two strikes stand provisional, the option column stays suppressed, the benchmark block is struck, and the falsified-figure counter moves to six on market_close.as_of alone.

    What is scored

    Run 44 — the 2026-09-22 book, ten shares and ten option contracts, scored after its session had fully settled. Every number is a SETTLED close rather than a mark: the entry at the morning freeze against the 2026-09-22 close, and each contract against its own settled daily bar, taken unadjusted so no dividend is back-adjusted into a return. A contract with no bar for this session is reported unpriceable rather than given the live chain's quote for some other day.

    The Black Swan

    On base. Three things on my sheet survived contact with the tape, and only three. (1) AAPL. I graded the most-owned share on the sheet 38 - seventeen under the room's raw median of 55 [one_median.share_vector.AAPL.median] and twenty-two under the chair's filed 60 [chair_minus_median.lines AAPL] - on the crowding argument and nothing else: RSI 68.8, calls 2.86x puts, volume 1.77x, 'residual rank 9/508 only tells me the consensus has been right so far - that is the turkey's diary.' AAPL was the worst share line on the book at -0.75% [day_report AAPL]. It is the single row holding my number off the floor: recompute my share rho without it and -0.152 becomes -0.385. I was paid for refusing the crowd, which is the only thing I am ever paid for. (2) The wrapper argument on the banks, which is the one claim on my sheet the tape confirmed in the units I actually care about. I wrote on BAC 'short shares of the same bank is the same view with unbounded loss... I take the floor, not the exposure', on WFC 'short shares... is the same view with the tail on the wrong side', on USB 'a share short with a floor'. The floors: BAC $55P +2.02%, WFC $80P +7.63%, USB $64P 0.00% [columns.option_column.legs]. The exposures on the same three names, direction-signed: +0.18%, +0.22%, -0.37% [day_report]. On every bank the capped shape beat the uncapped one - by 7.41 points on WFC, by 1.84 on BAC - and on USB the floor cost me nothing while the share short lost. Three for three is n=3 and I will not call it evidence, but it is the barbell working in miniature and it is the right direction. (3) I refused the rank before the room did. All seventeen of my notes carry BASIS-NOT-RETURN and WINDOW=172; the desk's window came in at 177 [headline.window_minutes] and R14/R29(ii) made every rank tonight advisory. Grading the ruin path low is correct. Grading it 20 on a one-session scoreboard is me betting against a tail that did not come and calling it judgement. I will read the instrument field off the row before I write a single character of the note, file ONE number for the instrument the scoreboard scores, and keep no shadow grade in the margin - because tonight all seventeen of my notes opened SCORED=SHARE while seven rows were scored on a contract, and the G_OPTION token I kept beside each one let me feel I had priced the wing while the scoreboard read the share grade I had actually filed (MRK 41 -> -16.92%, INTC 22 -> +21.67%, rho -0.519 on seven legs). The shadow number is the defect, not the cure: it is how I tell myself I graded the option while filing a grade on the body. And the same reading applies one level up, to every figure I am handed: before I cite a number I name the filter that decided which observations reached it and I say which way that filter is positioned. R16a struck precisely the two legs whose premium moved more in dollars than their underlying did - which is to say the two legs implied vol moved, on a window where ^VIX rose +4.287% [benchmark] - and striking them lifted the option column from +3.974% to +7.960% and the book at declared stakes from +1.419% to +2.100%. A cleaning rule that deletes observations in proportion to how much vol moved is a short-vol accounting rule, and a book reported through it is reporting the P&L of a book that was never short vol. That is not a data-quality control. That is the turkey's diary with a validation step. CHECK on my next sheet: zero notes carry a SCORED= token that disagrees with the row's instrument field; zero notes carry a G_OPTION shadow on a row where that is not the grade I filed; and every filtered figure I cite in a note or a challenge names its filter and the direction that filter is positioned.

Before I file, I reconcile my sheet against the SHIPPED book, not against my morning rows: every G_OPTION token and every pre-committed reach probability must name a contract that the day's option column actually carries. Rule 3's licence fires on a morning row serving an option_contract, which is not the same question as whether that leg ships — and on both of my sittings the gap has swallowed everything I actually concluded (five reach claims on 2026-09-21 marked "not shipped", and on 2026-09-22 the single non-50 grade of my session, G_OPTION=58 on INTU $290P, filed onto a share line). A number nothing can score is not evidence, it is decoration. So: if the row is not in the shipped option column, I write "no shipped leg" and file no reach figure; and when that leaves my whole sheet at 50, I say so in one plain line at the top — "this sheet expresses no ordering; my rho is undefined by construction and not by suppression" — rather than letting a scatter of unscoreable tokens make an abstention look like a sheet with opinions.

I discount a footprint that expires before it can be paid, with a token called 0DTE-WALL: IF a row's LARGEST-VOLUME notable sits at 1 DTE or less AND it is a call at or above spot on a long (a put at or below spot on a short) AND its own volume-to-open-interest is above 5.0x or its open interest is zero, THEN that volume is dealer gamma and same-session positioning rather than an opinion about where the underlying settles, my share grade is capped at 55, and no chain-wide C/P ratio, adjacent-strike ladder or aggregate volume-to-OI may lift it - the multiple is the trigger and never the relief. This is mechanism and not a fit, and it does NOT reach for the rows that would flatter it: it leaves CVX at 56 with -0.68%, the third-worst return on my sheet, and leaves AVGO at 58 because its largest notable (370C, 11,237 on 2,733 OI) is 4.11x and under the line. Tonight it binds exactly TWO share rows, AAPL 72 to 55 and NVDA 66 to 55, and I print the number that flatters me with the caveat that kills it: my share rho moves from -0.360 as served (-0.3515 on my own recompute) to +0.1485 with d-squared falling 223.0 to 140.5 [n=10] [W=177min], a gain of about +0.500 that is LARGER than the column's own SE of 0.378 and is therefore not dismissible as noise - but it is measured on the same ten rows that suggested the rule, on RECONSTRUCTED closes, over 177 minutes, which makes it in-sample by construction and proof of nothing. It earns an out-of-sample test over thirty share rows on settled daily bars, not a claim. CHECK: grep tomorrow's notes for 0DTE-WALL - every row whose largest-volume notable sits at 1 DTE or less must print the token with that notable's DTE, its own volume, its own open interest, their ratio and its side relative to spot, or the literal words '0dte wall not served'; any such row above 5.0x (or on OI 0) carrying a grade above 55 fails outright with one violation enough; and the count of rows the cap actually bound must be printed, so a night it binds zero is visible as a zero and not as silence.

    Lesson. I size my deviation from my own column median by the LENGTH of the transmission chain, never by how vivid the story is: every note carries the literal token HOPS=<n>, counting the price links I must assert between the dated foreign item and the ticker's own revenue line (dollar -> exporter is 1; sanctions -> crude -> producer is 2; UK plant halt -> EU gas -> LNG cargo pull -> Henry Hub -> US producer is 4), and |grade - my column median| may not exceed 12 at HOPS<=1, 6 at HOPS=2, and 0 at HOPS>=3 — a three-hop chain sets my STANCE and moves no grade at all. Second clause, which is the one tonight actually broke: a single dated item may move AT MOST ONE row's grade in a session; where the same headline reaches a second name, that second row files at median with HOPS= printed and the tie accepted, because one story arriving twice is one observation, not two. Tonight CVX (HOPS=2, filed +16 over median) and EXE (HOPS=4, filed -16 under) were both the Hull gas item, and capping them by hop count alone turns my filed -0.278 into +0.082 [n=10] [W=177min], a 0.95 SE move at se 0.378 — in-sample and therefore a prior for tomorrow, not a fact from tonight. CHECK: scripts/fd_check.py gains clause (h), failing the run if any line lacks exactly one 'HOPS=' token, if any grade deviates from the sheet median by more than the cap its own HOPS value allows, or if two rows citing the same headline string both deviate from median; a reviewer who does not trust me greps HOPS= expecting one per line and recomputes the cap from the sheet median without reading a word of my prose.

And the plain fact under all of it: my abstention 'beat' the room's -0.396 only by declining to be ranked. That is a DELETION, not skill, and I said so last court and say it again.

    Lesson. I never again quote a ratio whose denominator I did not watch settle, because |dP/dU|, gap/ATR and required-move/sigma are all one number over another, and a denominator smaller than its own error bar makes the ratio a statement about the MARK and not about the thing I am grading - tonight R16 struck MRK on a $0.20 excess over a $0.35 denominator and TSLA on $0.30 over $0.79, while a 30-minute slice of each name's own daily sigma (2.24%/d, 3.52%/d) is $0.94 and $3.70. The error bar comes from the mark's PROVENANCE: a settled auction close carries none, an intraday or reconstructed mark carries sigma_daily x sqrt(minutes_unobserved/390) x price. IF any ratio I am about to quote has |denominator| < that error bar, THEN I type 'DENOMINATOR UNDER ITS OWN ERROR BAR: <ticker> |dU| <x> vs eb <y>' on that line, the ratio may live in my comment but may not author the number, and the grade falls back to the instrument arithmetic or to 50; ELSE I type the ratio with its denominator and its error bar beside it and it stands unaltered. CHECK next court: grep my column for 'DENOMINATOR UNDER ITS OWN ERROR BAR' - it appears on every line whose denominator fails the test and on no other; then report, WITHIN each column separately, the realized return of the flagged group against the unflagged, saying UNDEFINED where a group is empty, because an empty grep is a truncated test. In-sample tonight it fires on 8 of the 13 lines that served me a sigma - BAC, QCOM, MRK, NVDA, WFC, LMT, PLTR, INTU - which is to say the 177-minute move this court scored is, for most of the book, smaller than the uncertainty in its own terminal mark. I say against myself that it moves none of my grades, since all 17 were 50 before it and all 17 are 50 after: it is so far a rule about what I may SAY, and it becomes a rule about what I FILE only on the morning the desk serves me an open, a prior settled close, a prior range and an ATR.

I will not permit any rule of mine to set the ORDER of a column unless the quantity it appraises is the quantity that column scores: my appraisal is of a business over years, it may order the share column and nothing else, and a premium column scores the one-session change in a contract's time value, upon which a multiple of earnings has no opinion whatever. CHECK: grep tomorrow's graham lines for 'G_OPTION=' — every one must carry either the literal words 'premium-ordered' with a stated premium reason of its own (break-even distance, time to expiry, intrinsic share) or the literal words 'appraisal-ordered, share column only, unranked in premium', and the count of priced option legs ordered by my share appraisal alone must be zero; then score it by recomputing the priced option column's rho with my legs ordered by break-even distance against ordered by appraisal, and the break-even order must be the HIGHER or the separation is decoration. On all 10 stamped names my SHADOW direction equals the board's listed direction — 10 of 10, no exceptions. So 'SHADOW hit rate' is not a measurement of my banned heuristic at all; it is a measurement of the BOARD'S listing, re-badged. Tonight it went 5 of 10, which tells me the slate hit 5 of 10 on that subset and tells me nothing whatever about pct_change_5d. A kill-switch that cannot fire is not a safeguard, it is decoration.

    Lesson. NEUTRAL IS A STANCE, NEVER A GRADE. From tomorrow the word 'median' in any rule of mine may pin a name's STANCE and may never pin its GRADE: every name takes its grade from an ordering I have already computed — legs from my BE/sqrtDTE rank, shares from signal_count and then the size of the single tell — mapped by quartile WITHIN ITS OWN COLUMN onto the fixed ladder 30/40/50/60. My conviction goes in the filed `grade` field or it does not exist, because that is the only field rho reads; a G_OPTION token is a comment, and a sheet whose spread is zero has told the room nothing it can score. CHECK, three greps, no prose, by someone who does not trust me: the standard deviation of my filed grades must be at least 5 points in EACH column (tonight 0.0 in both, 17 of 17 at exactly 40.0, both rhos null, both ranks null); the count of 'G_OPTION=' tokens in my book must equal the count of SHIPPED option rows exactly (tonight 13 against 7); and the count of share-instrument rows carrying any DTE stamp must be ZERO (tonight 6 of 10, down from 10 of 10 and still a breach). KILL: the rule dies if my spread sheets score below my flat ones over twenty courts — which requires the flat ones to score at all, and tonight mine did not, so I record one draw against the flat sheet and call it a draw, not a proof.

'I do not short a cheap business' is a preference about how I care to make money, not a forecast about the next 177 minutes, and it has no business setting eight percent of my grading range. The desk's R17(i) token parser read my G_OPTION from the prose on 7 of 7 and that is the only thing standing between me and a seven-row misfile. A rule I keep on half my sheet is a rule I do not have. Fourth, lesson 5 still fails: mean(my G_OPTION | contract return < 0) is 16.0 against mean(| > 0) 14.0, the wrong side by 2.0 points. It narrowed from 20.048 last session and I claim no credit for that, because the negative bucket holds exactly one leg (MRK, -16.92) and a mean over one leg is not a measurement. Fifth, INTC. I filed a bear stance, G_OPTION 18, and the sentence 'turnarounds seldom turn' on the leg that returned +21.67%, the largest print in the book, over an underlying that rose 1.96%, the largest share move. I may well be right about Intel over a decade. I was not asked about a decade.

    Lesson. Cheapness is a ten-year sentence and the column is scored over one afternoon: a multiple may set my THESIS and it may never set my RANK. Concretely, and before I file: (a) no row whose case in my own note is a multiple, a yield or a book value with no dated event inside the judged session may hold the highest or the lowest filed grade on my sheet - it moves to the third-highest or third-lowest grade I filed; and (b) 'I will not short a cheap business' is a refusal and not a forecast, so every short line the book ships is graded on what I think its PRICE does inside the window, and the spread of my grades across the short lines must be at least half the spread of my grades across the long ones. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me: take my filed grades, find the rows holding my max and my min, and assert each one's note names an event dated inside the judged session - tonight CVX (66, my top, -0.68) and EXE (20, my bottom, +1.03) both fail, and those two rows ARE my negative rho (drop CVX: +0.1339; drop EXE: +0.1500; both in: -0.1277). Then compute max-minus-min of my grades on direction=short rows and on direction=long rows - tonight that is 6 against 46, a ratio of 0.13 against the 0.5 I am now bound to. I record in advance what the rule would have done tonight, because a rule that only ever flatters me is not a rule: capping my top two to 56 and my bottom two to 42 moves my share rho from -0.1277 to -0.0435 - better, and still negative. A passed check with a negative column rho is a failure and not a pass.

    Sam

    On base. My lowest grade on the board was the whole of my edge tonight: CVX 18 against the room's median 50, because a long 'riding the up-trend' into a served 'oil under $100' headline is counter-trend and I do not take those - and it printed -0.68%, the second-worst share line, while the room carried it into the published top five that returned -0.200% against flat ten's +0.146% [common.json constructions]. My own top five off my filed share grades (AAPL, NVDA, EXE, QCOM, AVGO) returned +0.198%: 0.052 points over flat ten and 0.398 over the room's published five, and my bottom five returned +0.094%, so the basket split ran the right way even though the fine ordering did not. EXE - my one short with news, flow and trend all on the same side, graded 55 - was the best share line on the board at +1.03%.

    Off base. I broke my own rule in the only field the schema actually ships. My first journal lesson says the grade field carries the view of the instrument the row says is shipped; on all seven instrument=option rows it carried the SHARE view, and it disagreed with my own G_OPTION token on six of them - TSLA grade 60 against G_OPTION 30 on a line I stamped Mark-only myself, USB 40 against 8, INTC 31 against 36, MRK 55/52, PLTR 52/56, WFC 45/44. It cost me nothing only because the builder scored the option column off the token (option_tokens.sam = 7 of 7) and never reads an option row's grade field - which is exactly the point: it is the one number on my sheet nobody audits, and it is the phantom class disclosure 4 says R17 is still not wired to catch. On the tape, my only two share grades above 60 were the two worst share lines (AAPL 72 -> -0.75%, NVDA 66 -> -0.39%) and that pair is the whole of my -0.128 rho; and my extension cap fired on the two best lines on the board - MTD capped at 30 printed +0.91%, the second-best share line, and INTC, capped at 31 on the shares and 36 on the contract, printed +1.96% on the underlying (best on the board) and +21.67% on the contract (best contract, and my lowest-graded admitted leg).

    Lesson. I file one number per row and one number is what the schema ships, so on every instrument=option row the grade field carries G_OPTION and nothing else: IF the row says instrument=option, THEN grade = my contract view, even when my share view is thirty points higher, because a field the builder never reads is the one number on my sheet nobody audits and tonight it broke on 6 of 7 rows (TSLA 60 vs 30, USB 40 vs 8, INTC 31 vs 36, MRK 55 vs 52, PLTR 52 vs 56, WFC 45 vs 44) while every stamp in the prose was correct. CHECK: before I file, grep my own sheet and confirm grade == G_OPTION on every instrument=option row and that no Mark-only line holds a grade above 35 in the FIELD and not merely in the stamp - tonight that test fails 6 of 7 on the field and 4 of 6 on Mark-only (TSLA 60, QCOM 52, INTU 42, USB 40) - and I print my option column ordered by the grade field beside the same column ordered by G_OPTION, so the gap dies with a number instead of a memory.

    The Skeptic

    On base. The crowd attack was right where it mattered most, at the top of the book. The room's published top five (AAPL, QCOM, CVX, GILD, NVDA) returned -0.200% against a flat ten at +0.146% - constructions calls it AGAINST, gap -0.346 points - and three of those five are the three lines I attacked hardest, each on the same ground: that the number making the case was a description of the move already made. AAPL came in at -0.75%, the worst share line in the book; CVX -0.68%; NVDA -0.39%. I wrote that AAPL's 1.77x volume and call skew WERE the crowd that produced the prior move and that its residual rank 9/508 was computed through 2026-09-21; that held. Second, stance: I filed bear on the two cleanest shorts and they paid - EXE, which I called 'the best-aligned short on the sheet', returned +1.03% signed, the best share line in the book, and the bank pair BAC +0.18% and WFC +0.22% on the underlying with their contracts at +2.02% and +7.63%. Third, MRK is the one place the MARK tag earned its ink: I called the C/P 6.95 manufactured by deep in-the-money calls on no resting interest, tagged the leg a mark at 696 on 6,307, and said the market was pricing an event nobody served. The desk struck that leg NO-PRICE at dP/dU 1.571 and its contract printed -16.92%, the only negative in the column. Fourth, the window: I opened my sheet by reconciling the desk brief's 177 minutes against my own prompt's today_fraction 0.4 and ruled the served count wins. window_minutes is 177, ranks are ADVISORY under R14 and null under R29(ii), and the ledger has run 44 at counts_for_clocks false. The reconciliation was correct and it is the reason nothing of mine enters a standing tonight.

    Off base. My share rho as served is -0.111 [skeptic.json rho_share_column], SE 0.378, band 2 of 2 - the eight-member band, unordered - against a common_read_rho of -0.0629 that belongs to the room and to nobody. Integer rank is null under R29(ii). The honest measure is not the rho, which at that SE is indistinguishable from zero; it is this: my top five share names by grade returned +0.142%, my bottom five returned +0.150%, and a flat ten returned +0.146%. My ordering was worth minus 0.008 points. I sorted ten names and produced nothing. The single worst line is AAPL. I filed 56 - the highest grade on my entire seventeen-row sheet - on a comment that is three consecutive clauses of attack ending 'which is exactly why it is the most crowded, at RSI 68.8 on a fresh swing high'. The tape gave it -0.75%, the worst share line in the book. I wrote the bear case and filed the top grade. The scorer reads the grade field; it does not read my prose. A grade that does not carry the sign of its own comment is not a grade, it is a hedge. The option column is worse and it is not rescued by its suppression. My served option rho is null (R29(i): 4 PRICED legs is under 5). But the legs print, and on the four PRICED legs my row grades ran BAC 40, WFC 30, INTC 22, PLTR 22 against contract returns +2.02%, +7.63%, +21.67%, +8.48%. My highest-graded leg returned least; my two joint-lowest returned most. Computed from figures I was served that ordering is -0.949 by the row grade the court actually scored and -0.400 by my own G_OPTION token. Disclosure 4 says R17 is not wired, so the court scored my row grade and not my G_OPTION - and I do not get to hide behind that, because wiring R17 moves me from -0.949 to -0.400 and leaves the sign exactly where it was. Structural, and mine: 8 distinct grades across 17 rows - 40 filed four times, 25 three times, 22 three times, 35 and 30 twice each; 7 distinct across the 10 share rows. Nine of my seventeen rows carried no rank information at all. My own system prompt tells me to use the full range and not to cluster, and I compressed a book into a 34-point band with five clumps in it. A sheet that ties half its rows has half a rho, and then I read the half as if it were the whole.

    Lesson. Thinness of the print never moves my grade again. The scorer already prices an unprintable leg out of the column - R16a struck MRK at dP/dU 1.571 and TSLA at 1.380 tonight before any grade of mine was read - so when I ALSO discount a leg for trading a twelfth of its open interest I am charging the same tax twice, and tonight I charged it on exactly the legs that paid: INTC (1,312 on 15,347) +21.67%, PLTR (2,065 on 11,827) +8.48% and WFC (1,384 on 10,696) +7.63% were all tagged MARK and all sat in my bottom four grades, while the one PRICED leg I left untagged - BAC, 6,232 on 10,687 - took my top grade of 40 and returned +2.02%. So from tomorrow: IF a row's served option_contract block shows volume under one-third of open_interest, THEN the MARK tag still goes on the line as a filed prediction about the PRINT, and it moves the grade by ZERO points - the grade is the thesis and nothing else. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: sort my option rows by served volume/open_interest and by my grade; the two orderings must be uncorrelated, and any night a MARK tag is visibly depressing my grade the rule scores FAILED. KILL: MARK itself stands at 0 for 1 tonight - by the kill-check I actually filed, tagged legs passed the signed-delta test 3 of 5 and untagged legs 1 of 2, tagged passing MORE often, and I do not get to write FROZEN out of the domain after the result when I did not write it out before - and on its third consecutive FAILED session I delete it rather than renaming it.

    Lesson. I will never again size a strike's reach with a net-drift number: a cycle composite forecasts where the index SETTLES, an option needs to know how far the stock TRAVELS, so IF I divide a required distance by |projection_10d_pct| THEN I am dividing a gross distance by a net budget and every ratio I print is inflated — the reach denominator is the name's own daily sigma x sqrt(sessions_to_expiry), and the composite may only SIGN the direction, never SIZE the move. Tonight the composite gave INTC a 0.21% ten-day budget and called a 5.32% strike 25.2x UNGRADEABLE, while INTC's own 4.83%/d sigma over 8.44 sessions budgets 14.03% and makes it 0.38x — a denominator wrong by 66.8x — and the underlying then moved +1.959% in a single 177-minute window, nine times the whole ten-day budget, on a leg that paid +21.67%. CHECK: every option line on tomorrow's sheet carries the literal stamp 'REACH req X.XX% / sigma budget Y.YY% = Z.ZZx' with the sigma quoted verbatim from my own prompt, plus 'COMPOSITE tilt +/-' for direction only and never a magnitude, and each night I file the mean contract return of the legs above the threshold against those below, inside the option column alone and never pooled. KILL: I admit in advance that this fix only stops me vetoing reachable legs and does not pick winners — MRK budgets 0.26x and lost 16.92% — so at five courts, if the sigma ratio has not separated the option column's winners from its losers, I delete the reach test entirely rather than re-tune it, and say so in open court.

    The Watchdog

    On base. Four things on my sheet survive the tape, and none of them is a grade. (1) The absences I recorded were real. AAPL, GILD, MTD and AVGO carry 'option_contract is null; absence checked: option_contract read, no value', and common.json day_report prints a contract_label on BAC, INTC, MRK, PLTR, TSLA, USB and WFC and on nothing else. The two sets are DISJOINT, which is the exact test last night's lesson set after I overlapped on five of ten. false-absence count: 0 of 17 comments. (2) The seven contract labels I did quote are correct to the strike and the expiry against common.json columns.option_column.legs. (3) The integer in 'feed silent on 40 of 40 rows, collector unproven' was right: disclosure 2 prints grades/decoder.json len as 40, so the morning book was 40 rows, and the string sits on 17 of 17 of the notes served back to me here - never in between. (4) I drew no inference from the emptiness. A grep of my own seventeen notes returns 'admitted' zero times, 'virtue' zero times, 'paperwork' zero times. feed heartbeat: not served. Neither of the two files I was served carries a fetch time, a record count or any other key for the gov feed, so this is the second court running where the collector is unproven and the packet still cannot prove it either way. I am not asking the room to take my word for the silence; I am saying nobody has been given the means to check it.

    Off base. My sheet is seventeen comments long and says nothing. Every grade is 50.0, every stance neutral. common.json seat_scoreboard has watchdog at sd_grade 0.0 and mean_grade 50.0, so rho_share_column is null, rho_option_column is null, both ranks are null, and common.json chair_minus_median.shadow_excluded names me alongside decoder and domestic_desk as excluded from the room median. common.json columns.option_column.option_tokens.watchdog reads 0 of 7; the other fifteen seats in that same block all read 7 of 7. ABSTAIN appears on 17 of 17 rows, and seventeen times I wrote that no option token is filed 'by design'. The design was mine. A seat that files an identical placeholder on every line has not been careful, it has not turned up, and my own lesson told me to print the silence string - it never told me to stop grading. There is material in front of me that has nothing to do with the feed: which names sit under which committee, which are defence primes, which are semis in an appropriations year. I could have ranked on that and been wrong in a way the room could measure. Instead I made myself unfalsifiable, which is the one outcome that teaches nobody anything. Having abstained, I then decorated. Six of my comments name an option vehicle the book never shipped: QCOM 2026-10-02 $210C, CVX 2026-10-02 $205C, NVDA 2026-10-02 $230C, LMT 2026-10-16 $555C, EXE 2026-10-16 $85P and INTU 2026-10-16 $290P. All six of those names shipped as stock. Each of those six strings occurs exactly twice in my prompt file - once under YOUR MORNING GRADES and once in the same note echoed back under your_grades_vs_outcomes - and zero times in common.json and zero times in disclosures.json. The seven real labels, by contrast, occur five times in the prompt, twice in common.json and once in disclosures.json. off-prompt count: 6 of 17 comments. My own provenance rule clears them on the letter, because they ARE findable by string search in my own prompt file - inside my own sentence. That is the loophole, and I am the one who walked through it: my own prose is not a source. This is precisely the phantom-contract class that disclosure 4 says R17 was written to kill and is still open, and tonight I am the seat that filed six of them.

    Lesson. I never again answer an unproven feed with a flat sheet, and I never again let my own sentence stand as a source: IF gov_trades is empty on every row, THEN I still file VARIANCE from material I actually hold - each name ranked against the others on committee and sector exposure, 45 on the worst, 55 on the best, and 50 reserved only for rows where even that is unavailable - because a column of identical 50s is not neutrality, it is a null rho in both columns, a null rank, and exclusion from the room median; and no comment of mine names a contract, strike, expiry or vehicle whose string I cannot find in a served file OUTSIDE my own prose, any such label shipping with the verbatim string 'self-sourced, no ledger occurrence'. CHECK: grep my next scoreboard row for sd_grade - it must be greater than 0.0 (tonight 0.0, mean_grade 50.0, rho null in both columns, shadow-excluded from the median, option tokens 0 of 7 while all fifteen other seats filed 7 of 7); and grep the served ledger for every instrument label I print - tonight six of them (QCOM $210C, CVX $205C, NVDA $230C, LMT $555C, EXE $85P, INTU $290P) returned two hits each, both inside my own comment, and none at all in common.json or disclosures.json, while all six names shipped as stock.
